- "What I, William James,[^31] said just now about the Absolute of transcendental idealism is a case in point.[^32]" — mechanical CROSS-SEGMENT [^31] -> @record, and support check "cut would do": kept. This is the author name span from the `source:` line, the one name span allowed outside the frame. A cut would not work here, because "I" is the subject of "What I said" and carries the claim. The span also resolves the later "I"s and "me" in the note.
- "Pragmatism may be a happy harmonizer of empiricist ways of thinking, with the more religious demands of human beings.[^1]" — weak: kept. The trimmed "I wish now to add a word in further explanation of the claim I made at our last meeting, that" is first-person framing and an outside-frame pointer. The quote still gives the hedged claim ("may be") as the source states it, and the capital P is allowed joining text.
- "Men who are strongly of the fact-loving temperament[^2] are liable to be kept at a distance by the small sympathy with facts which that philosophy from the present-day fashion of idealism offers them.[^3]" — dangling: kept. The check itself passes it. "that philosophy" is named in the same statement ("from the present-day fashion of idealism").
- "It is far too intellectualistic.[^4]" — dangling: kept. "It" resolves to the philosophy of idealism in the statement before it.
- "But,[^8] the brand of pantheism offered is hard for them to assimilate if they are lovers of facts, or empirically minded.[^9]" — dangling: kept. "them" resolves to the fact-loving men and the aspirants named earlier. The cut "as I said in my first lecture" is a pointer only.
- "It is the absolutistic brand, spurning the dust and reared upon pure logic.[^10]" / "It keeps no connexion whatever with concreteness.[^11]" — dangling: kept. "It" resolves to the brand of pantheism.
- "Be they what they may, the Absolute will father them.[^13]" — dangling: kept. "them" resolves to the particulars of fact in the statement before it.
- "But from the human point of view, no one can pretend that it doesn't suffer from the faults of remoteness and abstractness.[^16]" — dangling and cut lost content: kept. "it" resolves to the absolutistic conception the note has just described. The unselected concession ("Far be it from me to deny the majesty of this conception, or its capacity to yield religious comfort…") is not lost, because the note restates it in "First, I called it majestic and said it yielded religious comfort to a class of minds…". Adding the concession here would not help. It would come before the note's author name span, so its "me" would dangle, and an author name span cannot attach to "me".
- "It is eminently a product of[^17] the rationalistic temper.[^18]" — support check (cut): kept. The trimmed "what I have ventured to call" is the author's first-person framing. Reads-alone dangling on "the rationalistic temper": kept, false alarm. This is the author's own term, used as a name rather than as a referring word, and the next three statements spell out what it is (it disdains empiricism's needs, gives a pallid outline, and is noble in the bad sense).
- "In this real world of sweat and dirt,[^22] when a view of things is 'noble,' that ought to count as a presumption against its truth, and as a philosophic disqualification.[^23]" — dangling: kept. The cut "it seems to me that" is stance only.
- "His menial services are needed in the dust of our human trials, even more than his dignity is needed in the empyrean.[^25]" — dangling: kept. "His" resolves to "the God of earth and heaven" in the statement before it.
- "Now pragmatism, devoted tho she be to facts, has no such materialistic bias as ordinary empiricism labors under.[^26]" — dangling: kept. "ordinary empiricism" is a name, not a referring word, and empiricism is introduced in the note's first statement.
